title: Nurse-led heart failure clinic: what can be said about value before extending it to two more hospitals
subtitle: An economic question that the available evidence cannot yet answer
statement: The finance committee wants a cost-utility analysis of Hospital A's nurse-led heart failure clinic before funding it at Hospitals B and C. There is no comparison group, no utility data, a clinic model that has changed twice, and no usable published effect estimate for a nurse-led clinic in a regional hospital. The question is what can honestly be said about value now and what must be done so that a defensible economic evaluation is possible later.
whoAffected: Adults discharged with heart failure from Hospitals A, B and C (about 960 admissions a year), their families, the two nurse specialists, the cardiologists who sign off the titration protocol, and the finance committee.
whatHurts: Heart failure readmissions are frequent and distressing, and patients at Hospitals B and C have no nurse-led follow-up. A funding decision based on borrowed numbers could either waste money or withhold a useful service.
currentPractice: Hospital A runs the clinic; B and C discharge patients to general practice follow-up. Clinic activity is recorded in a spreadsheet; no utilities or costs per patient are measured.
whyNow: The finance committee meets in March 2027 and has asked for a cost per QALY.
patientCenteredGoal: People leaving hospital with heart failure get follow-up that keeps them well at home, funded on evidence that fits this region.
summary: Problem framed as a value question the current evidence cannot answer, with the design left to the Design stage.
